MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DATE OF BIRTH: [redacted]
MRN: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Peripheral blood
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic evaluation for suspected Fragile-X syndrome in pediatric male patient.

METHODOLOGY
PCR-based assay for detection of CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA locus). DNA was extracted from peripheral blood and analyzed using fluorescent PCR amplification with capillary electrophoresis for accurate sizing of CGG repeats. This assay detects normal, intermediate, premutation, and full mutation alleles in the FMR1 gene.

RESULTS
FMR1 CGG Repeat Analysis:
Allele 1: 30 CGG repeats
Allele 2: 31 CGG repeats

Interpretation: NORMAL

No expansion mutations detected in the FMR1 gene. Both alleles are within the normal range.

SUMMARY
Molecular testing for Fragile-X syndrome revealed normal FRAXA allele sizes with no evidence of CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene. Based on these results, the patient is very unlikely to have Fragile-X syndrome. The residual risk is less than 1% and would be due to rare point mutations or structural rearrangements not detected by this assay.

TECHNICAL NOTES
Allele Size Ranges:
- Normal: 5-44 CGG repeats
- Intermediate: 45-54 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

This test has been validated to detect expansions up to approximately 1000 CGG repeats. Rare FMR1 point mutations or deletions are not detected by this methodology.

Test performed by: [redacted name], PhD
Medical Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
